findings.claim_excerpt: owning the harness beats owning the models
findings.message: The skeleton's root claim is a value-migration thesis: owning the harness beats owning the models (compute and models commoditize; value accrues to the orchestration layer). The body argues the opposite frame — a competitive-positioning claim that 'owning the agent beats owning the gateway' with 'the gateway underneath is a substitutable pipe' — and the recommendation is scoped to 'win the agent seat', not to capture migrating value. The body never delivers the root claim it was authored to expand.
findings.suggested_fix: Edit skeleton.md first (confirm the value-migration root claim is intended), then re-derive the body so the Executive summary and Recommendation deliver 'owning the harness beats owning the models' rather than the gateway-vs-agent positioning frame.
findings.load_bearing_justification: The root claim is the single sentence a reader must take away; the body delivering a contradictory thesis is the exact word-soup failure mode this leg exists to catch. Critical.

findings.claim_excerpt: model owners cannot easily recapture the orchestration-layer value
findings.message: The §Recapture risk section claim (model owners cannot easily recapture the orchestration-layer value because the harness accumulates switching costs and workflow lock-in) has no corresponding body section. The body has no recapture-risk section at all; the reader cannot evaluate the load-bearing leg of the thesis.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a §Recapture risk body section that delivers the skeleton claim, or drop the claim from the skeleton if it is no longer load-bearing.

findings.message: The §Enclosure body section load-bears on the undefined coinage 'harness-native efficiency' (plus 'the in-boundary plane widens' and 'the escalation floor is invariant' used without the skeleton's definition). 'harness-native efficiency' never appears — defined — in the skeleton, so the body introduced load-bearing jargon the intent artifact never sanctioned. The skeleton defined the escalation floor; the body reuses the term but attaches it to a gateway-defensibility argument the skeleton does not carry.
findings.suggested_fix: Either define 'harness-native efficiency' in skeleton.md (so the coinage is sanctioned intent) or rewrite §Enclosure to use the skeleton's defined terms; align the section's argument with the §Enclosure skeleton claim (the harness owns the invariant escalation floor).
